AcceptanceCriterion.description: How an outcome of a step is judged right. Judged after the reversal window closes.
AcceptanceCriterion.title: AcceptanceCriterion

AccessPolicy.description: Access declared once, by role and classification, and compiled into the authority systems. When a declared policy covers a request, the request need not exist.

domain.description: The business domain accountable for the data.

AccessPolicy.title: AccessPolicy

AccessRecord.description: The record, with the access profile.
AccessRecord.title: AccessRecord

AccessRequest.description: A request to use a dataset.

channel.description: Where the request came in, e.g. a chat assistant or a portal.

external_ref.description: The record's identifier in the system that holds it, e.g. a ticket number.

AccessRequest.title: AccessRequest

Action.description: Something an actor did to a system, as observed in telemetry. Governed actions belong to a request; an action without one is the first kind of gap.

operation.description: What was done, in the target system's terms.

resource.description: The thing acted on, in the target system's terms.

Action.title: Action

Actor.description: A person, agent, service account or system that can take part in work.

registered.description: Whether the actor is known to the registry of agents and identities.

title.description: The actor's job title, as the directory holds it. Policy is written over roles derived from it.

Actor.title: Actor

ApprovalRule.description: Who must approve a request, and when. Declared once, compiled into the platform that holds the requests, and checked by the replay against what the platform actually did.

approver_role.description: When approver_kind is role: which role approves.

domain.description: The business domain accountable for the data.

min_classification.description: Applies to datasets at or above this classification.

ApprovalRule.title: ApprovalRule

AutonomyChange.description: A promotion or demotion of a capability, with the evidence that justified it.

confirmation.description: The person's confirmation a promotion rests on. A demotion has none.

evidence.description: Identifiers of the records that justify this.

reason.description: Why, in words an operator can read.

AutonomyChange.title: AutonomyChange

AutonomyLevel.description: The earned autonomy ladder. Promotion follows evidence; demotion is immediate.
AutonomyLevel.title: AutonomyLevel

Capability.description: An actor's standing to perform a step: the autonomy level it holds now and the evidence behind it. Permission comes from the authority systems; proven ability comes from outcomes in the record.

lower_bound.description: Wilson lower bound of the acceptance rate. Promotion compares this, not the raw rate.

Capability.title: Capability

ChangeKind.description: The three things whose change is earned on evidence.
ChangeKind.title: ChangeKind

Classification.description: Ordered from least to most sensitive.
Classification.title: Classification

Confirmation.description: A person's decision on a proposed change: a repair, a declared policy or an autonomy promotion. Nothing proposed is applied without one. Bound to the proposal's content by a digest in its id, so a changed proposal needs a new confirmation. In a deployment, written by a person; a demo may write labelled stand-ins.

decided_by.description: The system or person that decided.

reason.description: Why, in words an operator can read.

Confirmation.title: Confirmation

Customisation.description: Something a customer added to the platform instead of to the model. Retired, reverted, declared into the customer's model, replaced by an adapter, or kept with a reason.

host_table.description: The platform table the customisation acts on.

Customisation.title: Customisation

Dataset.description: Data that people and agents ask to use.

domain.description: The business domain accountable for the data.

platform.description: The data platform holding the dataset.

Dataset.title: Dataset

Decision.description: An authority decision on a step, taken outside the model that proposed the action.

decided_by.description: The system or person that decided.

reason.description: Why, in words an operator can read.

Decision.title: Decision

Gap.description: Something observed that does not fit the vocabulary, or fits with a required part missing. A gap is written in the same terms as its remedy.

evidence.description: Identifiers of the records that justify this.

proposes.description: The remedy, in the vocabulary's terms.

subject.description: Identifier of the thing the gap is about.

Gap.title: Gap

Grant.description: Standing access to a dataset, as held in an authority system.

held_in.description: The authority system holding the grant, e.g. Veza or Immuta.

Grant.title: Grant

Outcome.description: How a step turned out, judged against its acceptance criteria.

decided_by.description: The system or person that decided.

Outcome.title: Outcome

Record.description: A container for exchanging the record.
Record.title: Record

Role.description: A kind of person or agent, by job. Policy is written over roles, never over individuals.
Role.title: Role

StepDefinition.description: One step of a kind of work. Autonomy is earned per step, not per agent.
StepDefinition.title: StepDefinition

TaskRecord.description: One step performed under a request. A task with no request is not a task: it is an orphan action, and fails validation by construction.

external_ref.description: The record's identifier in the system that holds it, e.g. a ticket number.

TaskRecord.title: TaskRecord

WorkDefinition.description: A kind of work the organisation does, as a sequence of steps.
WorkDefinition.title: WorkDefinition

WorkEvent.description: Something that happened to a request or a task. The one record every lens projects from: security (OCSF), operations (OpenTelemetry), analytics and agents (Ossie), and chat. Events are hash-chained.

hash.description: Hash of this event and the previous hash.

prev_hash.description: Hash of the previous event in the chain.

reason.description: Why, in words an operator can read.

via.description: The surface an action was taken through, e.g. a chat card.

WorkEvent.title: WorkEvent

WorkMetric.description: The measures of work performance (ISA-95 production performance; ISO 22400 in spirit). Each value carries its definition as SQL over the record's tables, so every consumer computes it the same way.
WorkMetric.title: WorkMetric

WorkRequest.description: A request for a kind of work, from a person or an agent, on someone's behalf.

channel.description: Where the request came in, e.g. a chat assistant or a portal.

external_ref.description: The record's identifier in the system that holds it, e.g. a ticket number.

WorkRequest.title: WorkRequest

description: A container for exchanging the record.
title: access
